content.title: About
content.content: Boston Cream Pie is a classic American dessert consisting of two soft sponge cake layers soaked with vanilla syrup, filled with a smooth custard cream, and topped with a chocolate glaze. Despite its name, it is a cake rather than a pie.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dessert was created in the early 1900s and named after the city of Boston, where it first appeared in upscale restaurants.
In 1996, Boston Cream Pie was declared the official state dessert of Massachusetts.
The traditional recipe uses a custard made from eggs, sugar, milk, and vanilla, plus a dark chocolate glaze.
It is often served as bite‑size cupcakes known as Boston Cream Cupcakes.
Original sponge layers are lightly brushed with a simple syrup of water, sugar, and vanilla extract.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Milk and cream in the custard provide calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and dairy contribute riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from chocolate
items.content: Dark chocolate glaze contains flavonoids that may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cake contains milk and eggs, common allergens for some individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The dessert is rich in sugar, which can raise blood glucose levels and add extra calories.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: Some commercial chocolate glazes may contain partially hydrogenated oils.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boston Cream Pie is typically served in individual squares. It can be enjoyed chilled from the refrigerator or gently warmed to soften the chocolate glaze.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cake in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it tightly wrapped for up to 2 months; thaw in the refrigerator before serving.
